blend.lean: Celtic-heavy - a Germanic ruling house (Gund-) Celticized among a Celtic land and people

_note: Cross-family blend (Germanic + Celtic), leaning Celtic: a Celto-Germanic frontier realm - a Germanic warrior house (the Gund-) settled among a Celtic populace and largely Celticized. Backbone = Celtic (goidelic: phonology, the dun-and-rath land, druidic religion); overlay = Germanic (gothic: the ruling-house titles and war-band veneer). civ = feudal. NEUTRAL ALONE (a settled, custom-bound frontier folk). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Gaelic/Gothic registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Celtic primary, Germanic variant), never real gods.

phonology.palette: Insular Celtic (Goidelic) backbone (initial mutation; broad/slender consonants; -aj/-an endings) with a Germanic overlay (the Gund- dithematic ruling-names, -burg/-reiks); theophoric on the Celtic morphs (Toran-, Orlann-) with Germanic variants (Thulrs-, Erlands-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV/CVC; Celtic mutation-clusters; the Germanic overlay adds dithematic compounds and -burg.

morphology.patronymic_form: Celtic patronymic Mac- (son of) / O- (descendant of) and the fine (kin); the ruling Gund- house keeps a Germanic dithematic lineage (-ingos).
morphology.compounding_rule: [quality|feature](stem) + element: Dun-derg (red-fort), Mag-mor (great-plain); the Germanic overlay yields Gund-burg and the -ingos ruling lineages.

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Celto-Germanic realm: the Gund- ruling house over Celtic tigerns and flaiths; the brithem's custom-law binds, the war-band serves)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Celtic-leaning ladder, ascending, with the Germanic ruling-house at the crown. Bo-aire (cattle-lord) barony; Marca-tigern (march-lord; Germanic marca + Celtic tigern) march; Tigern (lord) county; Flaith (prince-lord) duchy; Ri-Tuaithe (king of a tuath) principality; Ri-Reiks (the Gund- king; Celtic ri + Germanic reiks) kingdom; Ard-Reiks (high-king) empire. The brithem (judge) and the drui (druid) stand outside the ladder. (Rank titles fuse the real Gaelic/Gothic register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: Celtic personal + Mac-/O- + fine (kin); the ruling Gund- house carry a Germanic dithematic name and -ingos lineage; deed/animal epithets.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Celtic populace keep Gaelic names; the Gund- ruling house Germanic dithematic names.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Celtic devotional names on the morphed stems (Mael- devotee, Gilla- servant): Mael-Toran, Gilla-Gaian; the ruling house adds Germanic -mers (Thulra-mers).

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon (Celtic primary, from family_celtic theonym_set; Germanic variant, from family_germanic reflexes), never real Celtic/Germanic gods. Gundic is Neutral alone: both power-sets are ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared - and largely set aside for the Tuath-de (god-kin), the Anses (deified ancestors) and the spirits of grove and place. The drui keep the nemed-grove; the Gund- house keep an alhs-grove for their forebears.
religion.the_one: Eternan (< Aeternus; Germanic variant Aiterns) - the Ancient One above the god-kin; acknowledged and set aside (Neutral)

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Toran (Gmc Thulrs) - the sun, the just brightness
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Realtan (Gmc Riala) - the mother, the mercy-star

worship_by_alignment.Neutral: all powers ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared; foreground the Tuath-de (god-kin), the Anses/ancestral dead, and the spirits of grove, well and hearth

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the wild Chaotic powers, feared and warded rather than worshipped, keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Maragan the War-Fire (Gmc Marahs); Vacidus -> Faicid the Unmaker; Lusanto -> Losand the Hoard-Worm.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Nemed (sacred grove) of [power] and the Gund- alhs-grove: 'the Nemed of Toran', 'the Alhs of the Gundings'.
religion.saints_pattern: the Tuath-de and the ancestral heroes of the fine, plus the Gund- forebears (the Anses), honored at the cairn, the holy well and the grove.

holy_symbol_motifs.Gaian: the green earth beneath the standing stones
holy_symbol_motifs.Orlann: an iron spear crossed with a torc
